user.t:
Phase 4 of the read-only "Hebbwise" research mission. Hebbwise is the working name of an open-source Claude Code plugin to cut AI coding agents' tokens, raise efficiency (fewer steps/latency/waste) and improve answer quality.

Working dir: C:\Users\mariu\open source project. Read ./research/README.md (SOP + Idea Entry template), ./research/03-techniques.md (31 rows T01–T31 + "Negative results to respect"), and skim ./research/02-projects-plugins.md "Gaps" section and ./research/01-mesh-hebbian.md as needed for detail.

Write ONLY ./research/04-plugin-ideas.md:
1. 5–8 distinct plugin concepts, each an Idea Entry using the EXACT template from README.md. Each combines ≥1 catalog technique (reference by ID, e.g. T03) and targets ≥1 of the axes token / efficiency / quality.
2. Scores 1–5 on all four: usefulness, feasibility, evidence-backing, differentiation. Evidence-backing must follow the catalog: ideas resting on measured rows can score high; ideas resting on claimed/unverified rows or on anything listed in "Negative results to respect" must score low (and say so). Differentiation must be scored against the installed overlapping plugins: token-shield, token-saver, ruflo-cost-tracker (cost-compact-context, cost-booster-route), code-parser — set Novelty to "overlaps <plugin>" where applicable.
3. "Why it works" must cite at least one real path:line (copy from 03; full ~/ paths, no aliases).
4. Then a ranked shortlist table: rank | idea | axis | total score (sum of 4) | novelty | key techniques. State a single top pick with a 2–3 sentence rationale, and note which ideas could later be folded into the top pick as extensions.
Hint (not binding — judge from the evidence): the largest measured lever in the catalog is lean subagent dispatch (narrow tools: lists; 3.8k–18k vs ~95k spawn context), and the main gap is that no installed plugin learns from outcomes. The Hebbian router only ties Thompson sampling, so don't sell "Hebbian" as the source of gains.

Rules: read only except that one file; no new factual claims beyond 01–03; no invented APIs. Report: the ideas with their 4 scores, the ranking and the top pick.

handback.t:
I wrote C:\Users\mariu\open source project\research\04-plugin-ideas.md. It is the only file I touched; everything else was read only. It holds 7 ideas, each in the exact Idea Entry template from README.md. Each idea has a "Limits" note under it, and every "Why it works" cites full `~/` path:line references copied from 03. The file also has a ranked shortlist, a top pick and a "considered and not proposed" list.

Scores are usefulness / feasibility / evidence-backing / differentiation, out of 20:

| Rank | Idea | Axis | Scores | Total | Novelty | Key techniques |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | **Lean Dispatch**: subagents start from a narrow `tools:` list, checked before dispatch, with savings measured per agent | token / efficiency | 5/4/4/4 | 17 | overlaps token-shield (its Lever 4 is advice only) | T01, T04, T11, T02 |
| 2 | **Catalog Trim**: agent and skill descriptions cut to 15 words or fewer, never lower | token | 3/5/4/4 | 16 | novel | T02, T04 |
| 3 | **Outcome Router**: learns which agent produces accepted results, per task type | quality / efficiency | 4/3/3/5 | 15 | novel (closes Gap 1) | T15, T14, T08, T09, T04, T27 |
| 4 | **Savings Auditor**: savings measured against a baseline, plus a quality gate | quality / token | 3/4/4/3 | 14 | overlaps token-shield, ruflo-cost-tracker | T04, T16 |
| 5 | **Targeted Reader**: index first, read line ranges, skip unchanged files, pack to a budget | token / efficiency | 3/4/2/2 | 11 | overlaps code-parser, token-saver | T19, T31, T30, T29, T16 |
| 6 | **Cache-Aware Switch**: adds prompt-cache rebuild cost to model and agent switches | token / efficiency | 3/3/2/2 | 10 | overlaps token-shield, ruflo-cost-tracker | T17, T22 |
| 7 | **Verified Cheap Tier**: deterministic $0 answers first, escalate when not confident | efficiency / quality | 2/3/2/2 | 9 | overlaps ruflo-cost-tracker | T12, T24, T21, T25 |

Ties would be broken by evidence-backing, then differentiation.

**Top pick: Lean Dispatch.**
- It rests on the largest measured lever in the catalog: subagents with a narrow `tools:` list start at 3.8k–18k tokens, against about 95k for all-tools agents (`~/neural-mesh/RD-LOG.md:379`). Trimming the forwarded prompt saves only about 350 tokens per delegation (`~/neural-mesh/RD-LOG.md:330`).
- No installed plugin shapes a dispatch mechanically; token-shield only advises it (02 Gap 2).
- It reuses existing code for the hook skeleton (T11) and the token ledger (T04), so every saving can be checked against real transcripts.

**Ideas to fold into the top pick later:**
- **Catalog Trim**: works on the same agent definition files Lean Dispatch generates.
- **Outcome Router**: once the ledger has an outcome field, it closes Gap 1, the main gap. It should run in shadow mode first and be benchmarked against the static keyword router.
- **Savings Auditor**: becomes the acceptance gate, the before/after report that 03 negative result 16 requires.
- **Cache-Aware Switch**: only after its claimed inputs (T17, T22) are measured.

**Evidence discipline:**
- **Lean Dispatch** gets evidence 4, not 5. The end-to-end −22.8% figure is labelled by its source as "n=5, confounded". 01–03 also never show whether a hook can rewrite a dispatch in place, so v1 should warn or block. Whether a narrow tool list ever starves an agent of a tool it needs is unmeasured, so it is flagged as an acceptance gate for the build spec.
- **Outcome Router**'s only real-data result is T15: a 69-row replay improved from .338 to .658. The other inputs are simulation results. How an "accepted result" gets detected is not defined anywhere in 01–03.
- **Low-scoring ideas**: ranks 5–7 rest on claimed or unverified rows, or run into the negative results (adaptive context size, answer caches that barely hit, the recall hook, the rejected local-LLM front end). Each entry says so plainly.
- **Hebbian**: I did not present Hebbian as a source of gains. The file notes that it ties Thompson sampling (0.7239 vs 0.7234) and uses Thompson sampling or the guarded router as the learner.
- **Not proposed** (each would rest on a negative result): recall-hook memory injection, an exact-match answer cache, a tool router for delegations, a local-LLM front end, adaptive retrieval-k, and a "Hebbian router" sold as a gain.

One naming note: the README file plan calls this file Phase 3, not Phase 4. The file header follows the README.
